title: Physarum learns and decides without neurons, and its behaviour is its morphological change

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Physarum learns and decides without neurons, and its behaviour is its morphological change

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The unicellular slime mould Physarum learns from repeated experience and makes decisions (e.g. growing towards the heavier of distant inert objects) without a brain, neurons or cellularization, and in Physarum behaviour is implemented as change of body shape, blurring the distinction between morphological and behavioural problems.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Beyond standard model organisms: stories of plasticity and change

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: These examples of learning and decision-making occur in the absence of a brain, neurons, or cellularization. From the perspective of evolutionary change across behavioral domains, one interesting thing is that for Physarum, its behavior is its morphological change.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind”, Animal cognition (2023), doi:10.1007/s10071-023-01780-3; section “Beyond standard model organisms: stories of plasticity and change”. Scope: Physarum polycephalum (slime mould)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-glue-01: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Habituation-like learning, choice, and morphological movement are measurable in published experiments. Existing records can test particular assays, while the general cognitive interpretation and the full breadth of behaviour remain only partially discriminated.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For repeated-stimulus assays, test persistent experience-dependent changes in response; for choice assays, quantify growth toward competing inert objects while controlling gradients and geometry. Time-lapse segmentation can determine whether locomotor decisions are implemented through changes in body morphology.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Object-associated humidity or mechanical gradients can confound choice.

Learning and decision-making have competing non-cognitive operationalizations.

Raw trial-level data may not be public.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.62
analysis feasibility: 0.72
data adequacy: 0.52
data existence: 0.62
operationalizability: 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Habituation and growth direction are standard measurements, and several independent Physarum papers report them, so a restricted test can be assembled from published results. There is no single open trajectory archive, and the mass result in particular needs its controls rechecked from the source paper. The identification of behaviour with morphological change is true of this organism's mode of movement and does not further discriminate the learning result.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure habituation as reduced crossing of a noxious region after repeated exposure, recovered by a dishabituation control, and measure growth direction toward inert objects that differ in mass. Reduced withdrawal plus reliable growth toward the heavier object would support the learning and decision results; no change, or growth explained by a chemical cue correlated with mass, would count against them.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Habituation protocols differ, and some replications have been disputed.

Growth toward mass can be a biomechanical taxis without a decision variable.

Raw trajectories are spread across papers and video supplements, not one archive.

data adequacy: 0.55
analysis feasibility: 0.5
operationalizability: 0.75
data existence: 0.5
